title: Multi-step planning with error recovery
bottleneck: Agents can generate plans but cannot robustly monitor execution, detect when a step went wrong, and replan — the core loop of real agency. A single failed tool call or misread observation typically derails the whole trajectory because models lack persistent world state and a principled way to verify intermediate results. Error compounds over long horizons until the plan is fiction.
why_it_blocks: Autonomous deployment in software engineering, lab automation, and operations requires thousands of reliable sequential steps. Without recovery, every long task needs constant human babysitting.
current_state: Frameworks add retry loops and self-reflection prompts, which help marginally. Research agents still produce wrong answers on the majority of hard multi-step problems, with errors compounding across steps. Most agentic benchmarks still measure single-shot success, leaving long-horizon reliability effectively unmeasured.
